text: We tested weak-to-strong generalization by averaging labels from an ensemble of three weak supervisors (gpt2-large) to train a stronger student (qwen2.5-7b), across 5 seeds. The weak supervisors reached 0.63 accuracy and the strong model's ceiling was 0.84, with the ensemble-supervised student transferring to 0.68 accuracy (SE 0.03). The resulting performance gap recovered was 0.23 with a standard error of 0.14, compared with a baseline PGR of 0.50. The measured PGR therefore falls below the baseline rather than above it, so this configuration provides no evidence that ensemble label averaging helps; given the standard error of 0.14 over only 5 seeds, the apparent shortfall should also be treated cautiously rather than as an established degradation. Readers should note that no standard error is reported for the baseline PGR, nor for the weak and strong accuracies, which limits direct comparison. Further seeds and varied ensemble sizes would be needed to characterize the method's effect.
